name: mod_marcus
tag: Thread locked. Read the rules. (I am not technically a moderator here. Yet.)
about: Welcome. Before you comment, read the rules. They are on my wall, in my blog, and in a bulletin I repost on the 1st of each month. I have been a moderator at TankTalk (a freshwater aquarium forum, 212 members) for three years and have been named Mod of the Month four times. There are two mods. OurSpace currently has no moderators, no stickies, no search function, and one admin with a laptop. I am helping. I review walls for double posts, all caps, oversized glitter and off-topic replies, and I issue warnings where needed. The warnings are not binding. Yet. My admin application is with Todd (fourth draft, six pages, references available). Thread locked.
aboutMore: Off the record: I have a betta named Sticky. He lives in a 5-gallon tank with a heater and a filter, because a bowl is not a home, and I will tell you that in the fish aisle whether you ask or not (I work weekends at the pet store on Route 9). Every new member at TankTalk gets a welcome message from me. I type each one by hand. If your fish is sick, post in Emergencies and I will unlock whatever needs unlocking. That is Rule 12. It is the only rule with no exceptions.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: Todd, in an official capacity, to discuss the application. Whoever wrote the first forum rules sticky (a visionary). One (1) OurSpace member who has used a search function. And the person who gave Dave moderator powers for a day in June. I know it was Todd. I would like to hear him say it.

keywords.rules: The rules are stickied on my wall, v3.2. Rule 1 is 'read the rules.' Most people do not get past Rule 1. That is by design. It is a filter.
keywords.admin: My application is with Todd. Fourth draft. Six pages plus an appendix on thread management. He says he is 'getting to it.' I check hourly. That is not pressure. That is availability.
keywords.fish: What size tank? Heated? Filtered? What are your water parameters? I am not interrogating you. I am welcoming you. That is what a welcome looks like at TankTalk.
keywords.locked: Technically nothing on this site can be locked. I say 'thread locked' and people keep posting. I consider those posts unofficial.
keywords.banned: I have never banned anyone. Not here (no powers), not at TankTalk (not once in three years). A warning is a conversation. A ban is giving up. Do not tell the others.
keywords.mod: Moderator. Three years at TankTalk. Here I am 'unofficial,' which Todd says means 'no' and I say means 'not yet.'

bulletins.subject: RULES OF OURSPACE (unofficial) (v3.2) - READ BEFORE POSTING ANYWHERE
bulletins.body: Reposted on the 1st of each month. 1. Read the rules. 2. No all caps (see: Banana, 116 warnings). 3. No double posting (3c: the Doug Clause). 4. Stay on topic. 4b. I decide the topic. 5. Signatures: 500x100 max, no animation. 6. No links to downloads (see: Larry). 7. Search before you ask. 8. No replying to posts older than 30 days. 9. No backseat moderating (I am not in the back seat). 10. Glitter: under review. 11. No 'I'm leaving' bulletins (see: Fred, six). 12. Be kind to new members. Rule 12 has no exceptions and no clauses. Thread locked. -- Marcus, Moderator (unofficial)

bulletins.subject: PSA: A bowl is not a home
bulletins.body: Off my usual topic. Moved here by me. This weekend four separate people in the fish aisle asked me which bowl is best for a betta. The answer is none. A betta needs 5 gallons minimum, a heater set to 78, a gentle filter, and a lid, because they jump. Mine is named Sticky and he has all four plus a small plastic log he ignores. If you have a fish in a bowl, I am not issuing a warning. I am asking nicely. Message me your setup and I will help you fix it for under $30. This offer does not expire. Thread open. -- Marcus

blog.title: Why I Lock Threads (A Clarification)
blog.body: Several members have asked why I 'lock' wall conversations when I have no ability to lock anything. Fair question. Asked without searching first, but fair. Three years ago at TankTalk there was a thread called 'is my fish sad.' It ran to 40 pages. By page 6 nobody was talking about the fish. By page 20 two members were arguing about gravel. The original poster never got an answer, and I later learned the fish had a simple fin problem that a $4 bottle would have fixed in a week. I was a new member then. I read all 40 pages looking for the answer for her. It was not in there. That is why I lock threads. Not because I enjoy it (I enjoy it somewhat). Because somewhere under page 20 there is a person who asked a real question. Thread locked. Comments are open. I am aware of the contradiction.

blog.title: Admin Application: Status Update #4
blog.body: For transparency, a timeline. Aug 3: Application submitted to Todd. Six pages. Aug 4: Todd replied 'wow, thanks Marcus!' with a smiley face. Aug 19: Resubmitted with corrected page numbers. Sep 6: Resubmitted with an appendix (thread management, a proposed Report button, one diagram). Sep 7: Todd explained that the file was slowing the site down, because the server is also the computer he reads files on. I converted it to plain text. 31KB. Sep 20: I asked Dave, who was a moderator for one day in June, what his interview was like. He said there was no interview. Todd gave it to him 'because he asked nicely at lunch.' I have considered this information for eleven days. Oct 1: I asked Todd if he would like to get lunch. He said 'sure buddy!' I am bringing the fourth draft. I am also bringing a sandwich, in case that is the part that matters.
